title: Shetland lace stole
subtitle: A lace-weight rectangular stole in traditional Shetland print o' the wave lace.
excerpt: A rectangular stole in lace-weight Shetland-type wool worked in the traditional print o' the wave lace pattern from the Shetland tradition. Cast on at the full length; all rows run widthwise. Finished size approximately 40 cm wide by 165 cm long, blocked. About 200 g of lace-weight yarn.
sourceNotes: The print o' the wave lace pattern (also known as cat's paw or feather-and-fan variant) is a traditional Shetland stitch documented in Sarah Don, The Art of Shetland Lace (1980), §Stitches, and in Sharon Miller, Heirloom Knitting (2004), §Shetland Lace Stitches. Both sources are in print; this entry uses only the public domain pattern structure, not Miller's specific charts.

glossaryTerms.definition: A traditional Shetland lace stitch with a flowing wave structure created by groups of yarn-over increases and matched decreases. The pattern produces a regular wavy motif across the fabric, characteristic of 19th-century Shetland shawls.
A length of smooth waste yarn threaded through all live stitches at a given row, allowing the knitting to be safely ripped back to that row.
Insert the needle through the next three stitches simultaneously from left to right and knit them as one. Creates a right-leaning double decrease.

content.text: A rectangular stole in lace-weight wool worked in the
print o' the wave
lace pattern from the Shetland tradition, to a finished size of approximately 40 × 165 cm. This is a sustained lace project: approximately 360 pattern rows at lace weight.
The pattern runs on an 8-row, 18-stitch repeat. Thread a
lifeline
every 50 rows without fail. Budget about 200 g (about 1,600 m / 1,750 yards) of lace-weight Shetland-type wool. A 2-ply or cobweb laceweight will produce a lighter, more translucent result.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 200 g (1,600 m / 1,750 yards) of lace-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3 mm (UK 11 / US 2.5) circular needle, 120 cm or longer

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: Several to mark the 18-stitch pattern repeats

items.name: Tapestry needle, scissors, blocking mat, pins

content.text: Gauge

28 stitches and 36 rows to 10 cm over print o' the wave lace on 3 mm needles, blocked. The stole body of 112 stitches (8 repeats × 18 sts / 2.5 reduction + 4 selvedge) gives approximately 40 cm width. At 36 rows per 10 cm, the 165 cm length requires approximately 594 rows.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast on

Using the long-tail cast-on over two needles held together (for a loose edge), cast on 116 stitches (4 selvedge + 9 × 12 sts body repeats + 4 selvedge). Tail: approximately (3 × 116) / 10 + 15 = 49.8 cm. Note the cast-on is over two needles; remove one needle before beginning row 1 so the cast-on is loose enough to block to the full 165 cm length.
Set-up border
Rows 1 to 6: work a 4-stitch garter selvedge on each side and a simple allover eyelet (yo, k2tog) across the body stitches. This sets the border before the main pattern begins.
Print o' the wave (12 sts, 8 rows)

RS Row 1: k4 selvedge, *k2tog, k1, yo, k3, yo, k1, ssk, k3; repeat from * to last 4, k4 selvedge. RS Row 3: k4, *k2tog, yo, k1, yo, k3, yo, k1, yo, ssk, k1; repeat from *, k4. RS Row 5: k4, *k3, yo, k1, k3tog, k1, yo, k3; repeat from *, k4. RS Row 7: k4, *k4, yo, k3tog, yo, k4; repeat from *, k4. WS rows (2, 4, 6, 8): k4, p to last 4 sts, k4.
Repeat these 8 rows until the stole length reaches 165 cm. Work 6 garter border rows before binding off.
Stitch count check-ins
After each 8-row repeat: stitch count must remain 116. The print o' the wave uses a
k3tog
which removes 2 stitches; 2 yarn-overs in the same repeat restore them. If count drifts, rip to the last lifeline.
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off. The cast-on edge was worked over two needles; the bound-off edge must match its elasticity.
Common faults

K3tog too tight: the three stitches are hard to get onto the right needle simultaneously. Use the tip of the left needle to lift the stitches slightly before inserting the right needle through all three.
Wave motifs not aligned vertically: the 8-row repeat alignment shifted between repeats. Check that the k3tog always sits directly above the previous k3tog position, not shifted by a stitch.
Blocking

Soak 20 minutes in cool water, press out in towels, pin aggressively to the full 40 × 165 cm. The print o' the wave motifs open fully only with firm pinning. Use very close pins along the long edges to hold the full length evenly.
Care
Hand wash gently in cool water, lay flat to dry. Lace weight dries quickly. Re-block after every few wears to maintain the full pattern definition.
What to try next
A full Shetland square shawl uses the same print o' the wave stitch. Work a separate edging knitted sideways, then graft it to the main body, the traditional Shetland finish for square shawls.
